issues.description: Fast-path regex lacks a stated invariant proving it never rejects a real CSS time token
issues.detail: The guard `HAS_TIME = /\dm?s/i` is a cheap pre-filter before the expensive `valueParser` call. For correctness, the invariant must be: 'every CSS <time> token contains a digit immediately adjacent to s or ms, so any value lacking that substring cannot contain a time value.' This is true for canonical CSS time syntax (<number><unit> where unit is s or ms), so the fast-path is sound. However, the invariant is unstated in code. A reader auditing this change has to reconstruct the proof themselves. One literate comment — 'every CSS time token contains \d immediately before s or ms; values lacking that pattern cannot contain a time' — converts an opaque optimization into a verifiable claim. Without the comment, this is UNDER-AUDITED.

issues.description: No measurement reported to justify the performance claim
issues.detail: The changeset reads 'Fixed: time-min-milliseconds performance' but no before/after numbers, profiler output, or benchmark on a representative corpus are included. The optimization is almost certainly in the critical 3% (valueParser is expensive; most declarations have no time component), but Knuth's discipline is: measure before optimizing, and report the measurement. A one-line note ('on corpus X, rule time dropped from N ms to M ms') would lift this from 'plausible' to 'demonstrated.'

issues.description: Constant name could more honestly reflect that the regex is a conservative over-approximation
issues.detail: `HAS_TIME` reads as a definite predicate, but the regex is actually `MIGHT_HAVE_TIME` or `LOOKS_LIKE_TIME` — it admits false positives (which are harmless, the slow path handles them) but no false negatives (which would be a bug). That asymmetry is the entire point of a fast-path and deserves either a name change or a one-line comment stating it. The literate-programming move is to make the asymmetry visible to the reader.

issues.description: Reordering of propertyName computation after the fast-path is sound but worth confirming explicitly
issues.detail: `vendor.unprefixed(decl.prop.toLowerCase())` was previously called unconditionally; it is now called only when `HAS_TIME` matches. Both calls are pure with no side effects, so this is a correct code motion. The only observable change is that `propertyName` is not computed for declarations whose values contain no time-like substring, which is the intended saving. Confirming this in the PR description or a one-line commit note would close the audit cleanly.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED but directionally correct. The optimization is a textbook fast-path: a cheap regex test that conservatively over-approximates 'value contains a CSS time token,' short-circuiting an expensive valueParser call. The invariant — every real CSS <time> contains a digit adjacent to s or ms, so the regex never produces false negatives — is sound but unstated; a one-line literate comment would make this verifiable by inspection rather than reconstruction. No measurement is included, which is the standard Knuth complaint about performance fixes: plausibly in the critical 3%, but the reader is asked to trust rather than verify. Ship it, but add the invariant comment and a benchmark number to elevate this from UNDER-AUDITED to RIGOROUS.
